items.stem:
|  | Complete portfolio | Incomplete portfolio | Total |
| Local applicants | ? | 48 | 84 |
| Remote applicants | 24 | 36 | 60 |
| Total | ? | ? | 144 |

Among the applications with complete portfolios, 2/5 were submitted by remote applicants. What is the probability that an application selected at random was submitted by a local applicant and had a complete portfolio?
items.stimulus: A university categorizes 144 applications according to whether each application has a complete portfolio and whether the applicant is local or remote. The results are shown in the table.
items.explanation: Let x be the number of local applications with complete portfolios. Since 24/(x + 24) = 2/5, x = 36, so the requested joint probability is 36/144 = 0.25.

per_choice.correct: Let x be the number of local applications with complete portfolios. Since 24/(x + 24) = 2/5, x = 36, so the requested joint probability is 36/144 = 0.25.
per_choice.trap: Choosing 24/144 reads the remote-complete cell instead of the requested local-complete cell; choosing 36/84 or 36/60 uses a conditional denominator rather than the total number of applications.

items.trap: Choosing 24/144 reads the remote-complete cell instead of the requested local-complete cell; choosing 36/84 or 36/60 uses a conditional denominator rather than the total number of applications.

items.stem:
|  | On time | Late | Total |
| Undergraduate program | 46 | 14 | 60 |
| Graduate program | 19 | 11 | 30 |
| Total | 65 | 25 | 90 |

Which of the following must be true?

I. The fraction of all reports that were submitted on time by employees in the undergraduate program is 46/90.
II. Of the reports submitted late, 11/25 were submitted by employees in the graduate program.
III. Of the reports submitted by employees in the graduate program, 19/90 were submitted on time.
choices: I and II only
II only
I and III only
I only
items.stimulus: A company records whether its employees submitted a report on time and whether the employees work in an undergraduate or graduate program. The results are shown in the table.
items.explanation: Statement I is a joint frequency divided by the grand total, so it is true, and statement II uses the late-report total as its denominator, so it is also true. Statement III incorrectly uses the grand total; among graduate-program reports, the correct fraction is 19/30.

per_choice.correct: Statement I is a joint frequency divided by the grand total, so it is true, and statement II uses the late-report total as its denominator, so it is also true. Statement III incorrectly uses the grand total; among graduate-program reports, the correct fraction is 19/30.
per_choice.trap: For statement III, using 90 as the denominator confuses a joint proportion of all reports with a conditional proportion among graduate-program reports.

items.trap: For statement III, using 90 as the denominator confuses a joint proportion of all reports with a conditional proportion among graduate-program reports.

items.stem:
|  | Test positive | Test negative |
| Actually positive | 78 | 12 |
| Actually negative | 9 | 141 |

What is the total number of test results that were incorrect?
items.stimulus: A diagnostic test was used on 240 samples. The accurate classification of each sample and the test result are summarized below.
items.explanation: Incorrect results are the samples classified as positive by the test even though they were actually negative, together with the samples classified as negative even though they were actually positive. Thus, the number of incorrect results is 9+12=21.

per_choice.correct: Incorrect results are the samples classified as positive by the test even though they were actually negative, together with the samples classified as negative even though they were actually positive. Thus, the number of incorrect results is 9+12=21.
per_choice.trap: Counting only false positives gives 9, and counting only false negatives gives 12. Both types of disagreement must be included.

items.trap: Counting only false positives gives 9, and counting only false negatives gives 12. Both types of disagreement must be included.

According to the table, how many of the employees surveyed both commute by bus and arrive before 8:00 a.m.?
items.stimulus: A company surveyed 90 employees about their commute and arrival time. The results are shown in the table.
items.explanation: The employees who both commute by bus and arrive before 8:00 a.m. are represented by the intersection of the bus row and the before-8:00 column. That entry is 18.
items.pattern: read an intersection from a data table

per_choice.correct: The employees who both commute by bus and arrive before 8:00 a.m. are represented by the intersection of the bus row and the before-8:00 column. That entry is 18.
per_choice.trap: The value 42 is the row total for everyone who commutes by bus, while 31 is the column total for everyone who arrives before 8:00 a.m. Neither total requires both conditions.

items.trap: The value 42 is the row total for everyone who commutes by bus, while 31 is the column total for everyone who arrives before 8:00 a.m. Neither total requires both conditions.

items.stem:
|  | Arrived early | Did not arrive early | Total |
| Bus | 18 | 12 | 30 |
| Car | 24 | 16 | 40 |
| Walk | 8 | 2 | 10 |
| Total | 50 | 30 | 80 |

If one of the 80 students is selected at random, the probability that the student traveled by bus, given that the student arrived early, is what quantity?
items.stimulus: A school surveys 80 students about how they traveled to school and whether they arrived early. The results are shown in the table.
items.explanation: Because the condition is that the student arrived early, the denominator is the total number who arrived early, 50. The desired probability is 18/50=9/25.

per_choice.correct: Because the condition is that the student arrived early, the denominator is the total number who arrived early, 50. The desired probability is 18/50=9/25.
per_choice.trap: Dividing 18 by 80 uses the grand total and gives a joint probability, while dividing 18 by 30 conditions on traveling by bus instead.

items.trap: Dividing 18 by 80 uses the grand total and gives a joint probability, while dividing 18 by 30 conditions on traveling by bus instead.

items.stem:

| Members | 18 | 27 | 45 |
| Nonmembers | 12 | 43 | 55 |
| Total | 30 | 70 | 100 |

Which of the following represents the percentage of all customers in the table who purchased electronics?
items.stimulus: A store recorded the number of customers who purchased electronics or groceries, categorized by membership status.
items.explanation: The percentage of all customers who purchased electronics uses the total number of electronics customers divided by the overall total: 30/100 = 30%.

per_choice.correct: The percentage of all customers who purchased electronics uses the total number of electronics customers divided by the overall total: 30/100 = 30%.
per_choice.trap: Dividing 18 by 45 gives the percentage of members who purchased electronics, and dividing 30 by 45 gives a percentage based on the member subtotal rather than all customers.

items.trap: Dividing 18 by 45 gives the percentage of members who purchased electronics, and dividing 30 by 45 gives a percentage based on the member subtotal rather than all customers.

items.stem:
|  | Acceptable | Unacceptable |
| Machine A | 24 | 16 |
| Machine B | 18 | 12 |

If one reading from Machine B is selected at random, which of the following is the probability that the reading was acceptable?
items.stimulus: A laboratory records the results shown in the table below.
items.explanation: Only the readings from Machine B belong in the denominator. There are 18 acceptable readings out of 18 + 12 = 30 total Machine B readings, so the probability is 18/30 = 3/5.

per_choice.correct: Only the readings from Machine B belong in the denominator. There are 18 acceptable readings out of 18 + 12 = 30 total Machine B readings, so the probability is 18/30 = 3/5.
per_choice.trap: Using the grand total of all readings gives 18/(24 + 16 + 18 + 12) = 18/70 = 9/40, which is an unconditional probability rather than the probability restricted to Machine B.

items.trap: Using the grand total of all readings gives 18/(24 + 16 + 18 + 12) = 18/70 = 9/40, which is an unconditional probability rather than the probability restricted to Machine B.

items.stem:
|  | Attended | Did not attend | Total |
| Freshmen | x | 28 | 40 |
| Sophomores | 18 | 22 | 40 |
| Total | 30 | 50 | 80 |

If the probability that a randomly selected student who attended the assembly was a freshman is 0.4, what is the value of x?
items.stimulus: The table shows the number of freshmen and sophomores who attended or did not attend a school assembly.
items.explanation: The conditioning group is the 30 students who attended the assembly. Thus x/30 = 0.4, so x = 0.4*30 = 12.

per_choice.correct: The conditioning group is the 30 students who attended the assembly. Thus x/30 = 0.4, so x = 0.4*30 = 12.
per_choice.trap: Multiplying 0.4 by the grand total 80 gives 32, and multiplying by the freshman total 40 gives 16; neither is the total of the conditioning group.

items.trap: Multiplying 0.4 by the grand total 80 gives 32, and multiplying by the freshman total 40 gives 16; neither is the total of the conditioning group.

items.stimulus: The table below shows the number of customers at a store classified by membership status and payment method. What percentage of all 120 customers paid by credit card?
items.explanation: The total number of customers who paid by credit card is 84. Since the question asks for the percentage of all customers, use the overall total of 120: 84/120 * 100 = 70%.

items.stem:
|  | Earned certificate | Did not earn | Total |
| Online | 48 | 12 | 60 |
| In person | 36 | 24 | 60 |
| Neither | 16 | 24 | 40 |
| Total | 100 | 60 | 160 |

If one student is selected from the students who earned a certificate, what is the probability that the student attended the course in person or attended neither online nor in person?
items.stimulus: A group of 160 students was classified according to whether the student earned a certificate and how the student attended a review course.
items.explanation: Among the 100 students who earned a certificate, 36 attended in person and 16 attended neither way, so 52 of the 100 students meet the condition. Thus the probability is 52/100 = 13/25.
items.pattern: read values from a two-way table

per_choice.correct: Among the 100 students who earned a certificate, 36 attended in person and 16 attended neither way, so 52 of the 100 students meet the condition. Thus the probability is 52/100 = 13/25.
per_choice.trap: Using the grand total of 160 as the denominator gives 52/160 = 13/40; using the total in-person row gives 60/160 = 3/8; and including all in-person students rather than only certificate earners gives 60/100 = 3/5.

items.trap: Using the grand total of 160 as the denominator gives 52/160 = 13/40; using the total in-person row gives 60/160 = 3/8; and including all in-person students rather than only certificate earners gives 60/100 = 3/5.

items.stem:
|  | Favor | Oppose | Undecided | Total |
| Members | 36 | 24 | 12 | 72 |
| Nonmembers | 24 | 16 | 8 | 48 |
| Total | 60 | 40 | 20 | 120 |

A person is selected from those who either favor the policy or are undecided. What is the probability that the person selected is a nonmember?
items.stimulus: A survey classified 120 people by membership in an organization and by their opinion of a proposed policy.
items.explanation: The restricted group contains all 60 people who favor the policy and all 20 undecided people, for a total of 80. Of these, 24 nonmembers favor the policy and 8 nonmembers are undecided, so the probability is 32/80 = 2/5.

per_choice.correct: The restricted group contains all 60 people who favor the policy and all 20 undecided people, for a total of 80. Of these, 24 nonmembers favor the policy and 8 nonmembers are undecided, so the probability is 32/80 = 2/5.
per_choice.trap: Dividing the 32 qualifying nonmembers by all 48 nonmembers gives 2/3; counting the qualifying members instead gives 48/80 = 3/5; and counting only nonmembers who are undecided gives 8/32 = 1/4.

items.trap: Dividing the 32 qualifying nonmembers by all 48 nonmembers gives 2/3; counting the qualifying members instead gives 48/80 = 3/5; and counting only nonmembers who are undecided gives 8/32 = 1/4.

items.stem:
|  | Volunteered | Did not volunteer | Total |
| Participated in music | 42 | 18 | 60 |
| Did not participate | 54 | 126 | 180 |
| Total | 96 | 144 | 240 |

A student is selected at random from the students who either participated in music or volunteered. What is the probability that the student participated in music?
items.stimulus: A survey of 240 students recorded whether each student participated in music and whether each student volunteered. The results are shown in the table.
items.explanation: The students in the specified group are the 60 who participated in music plus the 54 who volunteered but did not participate in music, for a total of 114 students. Thus the desired probability is 60/114 = 10/19.

per_choice.correct: The students in the specified group are the 60 who participated in music plus the 54 who volunteered but did not participate in music, for a total of 114 students. Thus the desired probability is 60/114 = 10/19.
per_choice.trap: Choosing 7/19 uses the intersection, 42, instead of the full music total; choosing 1/4 divides by all 240 students rather than the conditioned group; choosing 5/8 mismatches the music total with the volunteer total.

items.trap: Choosing 7/19 uses the intersection, 42, instead of the full music total; choosing 1/4 divides by all 240 students rather than the conditioned group; choosing 5/8 mismatches the music total with the volunteer total.

| Day shift | 19 | 11 | 7 | 13 | 50 |
| Night shift | 8 | 6 | 14 | 12 | 40 |
| Total | 27 | 17 | 21 | 25 | 90 |

If an employee is selected from those who completed at least 1 module, what does the fraction of selected employees who worked the night shift equal?
items.stimulus: A company records the work shift and module-completion status of its 90 employees. The results are shown in the table.
items.explanation: Employees who completed at least 1 module are the 63 employees outside the Neither module column. Of these, 32 worked the night shift, so the fraction is 32/63.

per_choice.correct: Employees who completed at least 1 module are the 63 employees outside the Neither module column. Of these, 32 worked the night shift, so the fraction is 32/63.
per_choice.trap: Using 32/40 reverses the condition by dividing by all night-shift employees; using 31/63 selects the day-shift count; using 32/90 divides by all employees instead of only employees who completed a module.

items.trap: Using 32/40 reverses the condition by dividing by all night-shift employees; using 31/63 selects the day-shift count; using 32/90 divides by all employees instead of only employees who completed a module.

items.stem:
|  | Renewed | Did not renew | Total |
| Basic | 27 | 33 | 60 |
| Premium | 21 | 19 | 40 |
| Total | 48 | 52 | 100 |

A renewal specialist chooses a customer from the group of customers who renewed. What does the quantity 21/48 represent in this situation?
choices: The probability that a randomly selected customer had a premium subscription
The probability that a randomly selected customer renewed
The probability that a randomly selected customer who renewed had a premium subscription
The probability that a randomly selected premium customer renewed
items.stimulus: A company reviews the subscription level and renewal status of its customers. The results are shown in the table.
items.explanation: Because the specialist selects only from customers who renewed, 48 is the denominator. The 21 premium customers in that group make 21/48 the probability of being premium given that the customer renewed.

per_choice.correct: Because the specialist selects only from customers who renewed, 48 is the denominator. The 21 premium customers in that group make 21/48 the probability of being premium given that the customer renewed.
per_choice.trap: The fourth choice reverses the conditional probability and uses 40 as its denominator; the third and second choices use the premium and renewal marginal totals, respectively, rather than conditioning on renewal.

items.trap: The fourth choice reverses the conditional probability and uses 40 as its denominator; the third and second choices use the premium and renewal marginal totals, respectively, rather than conditioning on renewal.

items.stem:
|  | Print | Electronic | Total |
| Members | 29 | 31 | 60 |
| Nonmembers | 17 | 23 | 40 |
| Total | 46 | 54 | 100 |

A librarian says that the quantity 29/100 describes a certain feature of the loan records. What does this quantity represent?
choices: The probability that a print loan selected from the records was made by a member
The probability that a loan selected from all records was a print loan made by a member
The fraction of all loan records made by members
The probability that a loan made by a member was a print loan
items.stimulus: A library classifies 100 loan records by the borrower's membership status and the format of the borrowed item. The results are shown in the table.
items.explanation: The numerator 29 is the joint cell for members and print loans, and the denominator 100 is the total number of records. Thus, 29/100 is the probability that a randomly selected record has both characteristics.

per_choice.correct: The numerator 29 is the joint cell for members and print loans, and the denominator 100 is the total number of records. Thus, 29/100 is the probability that a randomly selected record has both characteristics.
per_choice.trap: The first choice conditions on being a print loan and should use 46 as the denominator; the third conditions on membership and should use 60; the fourth uses the member row total and ignores format.

items.trap: The first choice conditions on being a print loan and should use 46 as the denominator; the third conditions on membership and should use 60; the fourth uses the member row total and ignores format.

items.stem:

| Members | 18 | 27 | 45 |
| Nonmembers | 22 | 33 | 55 |
| Total | 40 | 60 | 100 |

A theater manager says that the quantity 27/60 describes a feature of the customers who attended evening performances. What does this quantity represent?
choices: The fraction of all customers who were members and attended an evening performance
The fraction of evening-performance customers who were nonmembers
The fraction of members who attended an evening performance
The fraction of evening-performance customers who were members
items.stimulus: A theater records whether its customers are members and whether they attended a matinee or an evening performance. The results are shown in the table.
items.explanation: The denominator 60 is the total number of evening-performance customers, so the fraction is conditional on attending an evening performance. The numerator 27 counts those evening-performance customers who were members.

per_choice.correct: The denominator 60 is the total number of evening-performance customers, so the fraction is conditional on attending an evening performance. The numerator 27 counts those evening-performance customers who were members.
per_choice.trap: Using the members total of 45 as the denominator produces the third choice, which reverses the conditional probability.

items.trap: Using the members total of 45 as the denominator produces the third choice, which reverses the conditional probability.

| Under 25 | 17 | 23 | 40 |
| 25 or older | 31 | 25 | 56 |

An analyst states that the quantity 17/96 describes a feature of the residents. What does this quantity represent?
choices: The fraction of residents who received a notification and were 25 or older
The fraction of residents under 25 who received a notification
The fraction of all residents who received a notification
The fraction of all residents who were under 25 and received a notification
items.stimulus: A public health agency classifies 96 residents by age group and by whether they received a notification through a mobile application. The results are shown in the table.
items.explanation: The numerator 17 is the joint cell for residents under 25 who received a notification, and the denominator 96 is the grand total. Thus, 17/96 is the proportion of all residents having both characteristics.

per_choice.correct: The numerator 17 is the joint cell for residents under 25 who received a notification, and the denominator 96 is the grand total. Thus, 17/96 is the proportion of all residents having both characteristics.
per_choice.trap: Using the under-25 row total of 40 as the denominator produces the second choice, which changes a joint proportion into a conditional proportion.

items.stem:
|  | Used application | Did not use | Total |
| New customer | 24 | 18 | 42 |
| Returning customer | 36 | 22 | 58 |
| Total | 60 | 40 | 100 |

A marketing analyst uses the quantity 42/78 in a report. What does this quantity represent?
choices: The fraction of all customers who were new and used the application
The fraction of customers who were either new or used the application who were new customers
The fraction of new customers who used the application
The fraction of customers who were either new or used the application who used the application
items.stimulus: A company classifies its 100 customers by whether each customer is new or returning and by whether the customer used the company's mobile application during the month. The results are shown in the table.
items.explanation: The customers who were either new or application users number 42 + 60 - 24 = 78, since the 24 customers in both groups must be counted only once. Of those 78 customers, 42 were new, so 42/78 has the stated meaning.

per_choice.correct: The customers who were either new or application users number 42 + 60 - 24 = 78, since the 24 customers in both groups must be counted only once. Of those 78 customers, 42 were new, so 42/78 has the stated meaning.
per_choice.trap: Adding the new-customer total and application-user total without subtracting their overlap gives 42/102, represented by the common union-counting error.

items.trap: Adding the new-customer total and application-user total without subtracting their overlap gives 42/102, represented by the common union-counting error.
